connections.why: Specialised cells are adapted versions of the basic cell plan
Microscopes let us actually see the cells we describe
Similar specialised cells group together to form tissues
The skeleton and muscles are organ systems made of tissues
Digested food is absorbed into the blood for transport
Breathing supplies the oxygen respiration needs
Blood carries oxygen and glucose to respiring cells
Leaves are the plant organ where photosynthesis happens
Glucose made by photosynthesis is the fuel for respiration
Flowers are reproductive organs of flowering plants
Puberty prepares the body to be able to reproduce
Inherited differences are one source of variation
We classify organisms by shared and differing features
Producers at the base of food chains photosynthesise
Each habitat supports its own web of feeding relationships
Human activity destroys and changes habitats
